first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 FFO As Adjusted around $0.31/share. Sources: KeyCorp forecast $0.31 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/what-is-keycorps-forecast-for-akr-q3-earnings-2026-08-19/, 2026-08-19; the page itself only rendered unrelated headlines when fetched, so this rests on the search snippet) and Benzinga's table $0.31 with revenue $98.8M (https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/AKR/earnings-forecasts). FY2026 consensus is $1.24 per snippet. The company guide is FY2026 FFO As Adjusted $1.24-$1.26 (8-K ex99.1, 2026-07-28, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000899629/000119312526321040/akr-ex99_1.htm). With H1 at $0.61 ($0.30 Q1 + $0.31 Q2), that implies H2 of $0.63-0.65, or about $0.315-0.325 a quarter. Consensus therefore sits at the bottom of the guide-implied range. The bar comes from the company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so it is not capped.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest was 13,361,699 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 9.7% of 137.3M shares outstanding, with 10.42 days to cover. It is down from a 21.59M peak on 2026-06-15 and was 14.05M on 9-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/akr/shortinterest). No usable option chain (baseline options status no_paired_strikes), so there is no skew. An Unusual Whales snippet quoting a ±10.4% implied move is not credible against a 21% realised vol and the absent chain, and is ignored. Run-up: +1.6% over 5 days, +2.4% over 20 days, 16% below the 52-week high. That follows a 22.47 (July) to 18.74 (September) slide during a sector-wide rate selloff.

evidence.text: Acadia has lifted its 2026 FFO As Adjusted guide at every print this year: $1.21-1.25 originally, then $1.22-1.26 on 4/28, then $1.24-1.26 on 7/28. H1 was $0.61 (Q1 $0.30, Q2 $0.31 against $0.30 consensus). The guide implies H2 of $0.63-0.65, while Q3 consensus is $0.31 and FY consensus $1.24, the low end. So a Q3 of $0.31-0.32 plus a guide narrowed toward $1.25-1.26 is the likeliest release.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide raise with a beat on 2026-07-28 drew +2.21%; the guide raise on 2026-04-28 drew +2.12%. The FY2025 Q4 print on 2026-02-10, an EPS miss per secondary sources, drew -4.15%. The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-28) drew -0.16%. Seven-print median |move| is 2.12%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus has not moved off the low end of the guide ($1.24 FY), so the street is not modelling another narrowing toward the top. If it were, FY consensus would sit at $1.25-1.26 and Q3 at $0.32. The stock is also 16% off its July high despite the guide raise, which fits a rate-driven discount rather than an expectation of further raises. Caveat built into the size: Q3 itself lands inside the guided range, so only an upward narrowing adds anything.
evidence.independence: Q1 guide and result: 8-K ex99.1 2026-04-28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000899629/000119312526187104/akr-ex99_1.htm). The consensus figure comes from different sources (Benzinga, KeyCorp via MarketBeat).

evidence.text: The 2026-09-14 intra-quarter update reported $119M of Q3 REIT street-retail acquisitions (Greene St $60M, Bleecker $20M, Greenwich Ave $10M, Melrose $29M) and $742M YTD across the REIT and investment management. It also reported 12 new Q3 leases worth $4.8M ABR at share ($3.8M street retail), double-digit cash spreads, and 129 Fifth Ave leased within 30 days above underwriting at a yield on cost above 9%. No new equity was issued and about $352M of forward proceeds remain. Q3 operations were tracking the plan.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Leasing spreads and same-property NOI (+8.7% in Q2, street retail +15.6%) were the headline of the July print, which drew +2.21%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public, so mostly priced. What is not priced is how the leases and the $16.5M signed-not-open pipeline (Q2 release) convert into Q4 run-rate and 2027 commentary. The stock fell through September despite this update, during a sector rate selloff, which suggests the market treated company news as secondary to the 10-year yield.
evidence.independence: Commercial Observer on the Greene St purchase (https://commercialobserver.com/2026/09/acadia-buys-soho-69-71-greene-street/). Same company as finding 1 but a different document.

evidence.text: Shopping-center peers that reported in the week before the print raised their outlooks. Kimco (10-29) raised its 2026 outlook on record 96.6% occupancy and Q3 FFO of $0.47 vs $0.44. Federal Realty (10-30) raised and tightened Core FFO to $7.54-7.58 from $7.48-7.56, with 14% cash leasing spreads and its leased rate up 40bp. Retail tenant demand was healthy into Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline record of AKR moving on peer prints. AKR's street-retail mix (Q2 SP NOI +15.6% street) is more levered to luxury and urban tenants than KIM or FRT.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both prints were out before AKR's 10-30 close. It is filed as a sector proxy confirming no tenant-credit surprise. If the market had worried about AKR-specific demand, AKR would have lagged peers after their prints. Instead its 5-day run-up is +1.6%.
evidence.independence: Kimco Q3 2026 8-K ex99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000879101/000119312526436941/kim-ex99_1.htm), 2026-10-29. A proxy, not AKR's own number.

evidence.text: Short interest was 13.36M shares on 2026-10-15, about 9.7% of 137.3M shares outstanding, with 10.4 days to cover on a stock trading about 1.1M shares a day. A clean print with a guide narrowed upward meets a short base that needs ten sessions to cover.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest fell from 21.6M (June) to 12.0M (August) around the July beat-and-raise, which drew +2.21%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Days to cover above 10 is an amplifier rather than a direction. It matters only if the print is clean, and the baseline (no option chain) carries no positioning statement at all.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: AKR's drawdown from $22.47 (July) to $18.74 (September) coincided with the 10-year Treasury yield reaching 5.27% at the end of September, its highest in about 25 years, and REITs falling 5.7% in September. It is a sector rate move, not a company-specific cause. Rates over the window are a two-sided risk the print cannot settle.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on file.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is priced: this explains the drawdown and does not predict the print. It is filed so the judges can see the drawdown has a non-company cause.
evidence.independence: Price path from https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/AKR/price (monthly closes).

evidence.text: About $352M of unsettled forward equity remains (17.8M shares / $369M at 6/30 per the Q2 release; $352M at 9/14). It funds the REIT acquisition pipeline and the Henderson Ave development, 'fully funded, on a forward basis'. The money buys street-retail assets leasing at double-digit spreads and a yield on cost above 9%, so this is funding a visible ramp, not distress. Settlement dilution is a 2027 per-share question rather than a Q3 one.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 $200M forward offering came in the same quarter as the guide raise; the stock rose +2.21% on that print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Known and disclosed. Answering what the money buys (accretive street retail with corroborating leasing) signs this at zero.
evidence.independence: The 9/14 update (https://earningswhispers.com/article/AKR/2609143342) confirms no new equity in Q3 and $352M remaining. That shares a company with findings 1 and 2.

evidence.text: The Q3 2026 release moves to before the open on 11-02 with an 11:00 ET call the same day; all seven prior prints were after the close. This shortens the window in which the release is digested before the scored close.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior bmo prints in the baseline history.
evidence.why_not_priced: Not directional. It means the full call is inside the scored session, so the reaction should be more complete than after a pre-market-only digestion.
evidence.independence: none

first_hunter_context.bar: Company Q3 2026 guide from the 2026-07-30 call (transcript): revenue $665-685M, subscription $332-343M, non-GAAP EPS $2.43-2.53, adj. FCF $235-265M (https://www.webull.com/news/15364638754350080). FY2026 revenue $2.77-2.85B after the Q1 cut (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/check-point-software-technologies-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-04-30/), with FY non-GAAP EPS $10.05-10.85 reaffirmed. Consensus non-GAAP EPS is $2.49 (Benzinga, https://es.benzinga.com/quote/CHKP/earnings-forecasts). Revenue consensus sources conflict: $672M at Benzinga, against stale pre-guide figures of $695-697M at MarketBeat and goldesel. The calendar's $1.99 EPS (EarningsWhispers) matches neither the non-GAAP nor the implied GAAP guide (~$1.73-1.83) and is disowned. The bar used is the company guide midpoint, $675M / $2.48. The operative bar is the implied Q4: FY midpoint $2.81B less H1 $1,342M (668+674) less Q3 mid $675M = ~$793M, +6.5% on Q4-25's $745M. The CFO confirmed ~ $800M on the Q2 call.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest ~5.8M shares, 4.9 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement (down from 6.2M / 5.5d at 09-15), per https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/chkp/short-interest/. Swingtradebot shows ~8.1% of float and 5.97 DTC around 2026-10-21 (https://swingtradebot.com/equities/CHKP). Moderate, not crowded. Baseline skew_25d is -3.39 vol points (25d calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'), put/call OI 0.53, event-implied move 9.08%, ATM IV 58.7%. Tape (Yahoo chart): 137.87 on Oct-16, then +15% in three sessions Oct 21-23 to 159.03 on a sector rally; 159.84 on Oct-27; -2.9% Oct-28; opened -4.5% Oct-29 on the FTNT print and closed -1.1% at 153.50; ~149 intraday Oct-30. 20d run-up +13.85%, 5d -6.68%, 27% below the 52-week high.

evidence.text: Two direct hardware-security peers reported the September quarter this week, beat, and fell ~20% each on forward commentary. F5 (Oct-27 amc): systems revenue +29% and revenue $917M above its $870-890M guide, but FY27 growth was guided to 8-9% with gross margin pressured by memory and component costs; the stock went 459.36 to 365.53 (-20.4%) and was ~335 intraday Oct-30. Fortinet (Oct-28 amc): product +37%, billings +29%, guide raised; but management said H1 product benefited from on-hand inventory that normalized in Q3, product gross margin is under cost pressure, and pricing was ~10pp of billings growth; FTNT went 174.08 to 139.10 (-20.1%). Check Point has its own memory-cost headwind (~1pt GM in 2026, mostly H2) and 300 sales hires for 2027, so its call will be read for the same Q4 and 2027 margin questions. So far it has absorbed only ~-7% off its Oct-27 high.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHKP's last three prints all moved on the forward revenue guide, not the EPS beat: Feb-12-2026 -6.8% (176.47 to 164.47), Apr-30-2026 -19.6% (139.96 to 112.47, FY revenue cut), Jul-30-2026 -8.2% (139.67 to 128.23, Q3 guide below consensus despite EPS $2.55 vs $2.45). Prices from Yahoo chart v8.
evidence.why_not_priced: On Oct-29 CHKP opened -4.5% on the FTNT read and closed only -1.1%. It remains +8% above where it started the Oct-21 sector rally. Calls are still bid over puts (skew -3.39). If the market had carried the peers' de-rating into CHKP, it would be back near ~138 with put skew positive.
evidence.independence: F5 is a separate document pointing the same way: FY27 growth decel and memory-driven gross-margin compression, -20.4% on a beat (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001048695/000104869526000074/ex991-q426earningsreleasef.htm and https://www.quiverquant.com/news/F5+Slides+as+2027+Margin+Outlook+and+Growth+Pace+Temper+Strong+Q4+Results). CHKP's own memory GM headwind: https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/12/no_fire_sale_on_firewalls/. This is a proxy, macro-to-company transmission that CHKP has not confirmed for 2027.

evidence.text: The same peer prints show strong September-quarter appliance demand: Fortinet product +37% with $1M+ deals up 51% and 'no slowdown in demand'; F5 systems +29%. Check Point guided its Q3 product line to trend like Q2's -14% and assumed large appliance deals slip from Q3 to Q4. That is a deliberately conservative assumption in a strong market, which raises the odds that Q3 revenue lands at or above the $675M guide midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: CHKP beat Q2 revenue ($674M vs ~$675M consensus/at-guide) and EPS ($2.55 vs $2.45) and fell 8.2% on the guide. A reported-quarter beat has not been paid on any of the last three prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of ~$2.49 and revenue of ~$672M sit at the CHKP guide midpoint and were set before either peer reported. Peer-informed upward revisions would show as revenue consensus at the top of the guide; none has been found.
evidence.independence: F5 8-K systems +29% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001048695/000104869526000074/ex991-q426earningsreleasef.htm). Caveat already netted into the size: a channel analyst cited in German press says CHKP is not benefiting from firewall demand at the same pace as competitors, and CHKP's issue has been its own go-to-market disruption (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/check-point-verlagert-deals-in-q4-und-halt-fy26-guidance-q3-eps-soll-uber-konsens-liegen). This shares the Fortinet documents with finding 1 but reads a different line (Q3 demand, not forward margin).

evidence.text: The held FY2026 revenue range of $2.77-2.85B implies Q4 of ~$753-833M, ~$793M at the midpoint (+6.5% on Q4-25's $745M). The CFO confirmed ~ $800M on the Q2 call, resting on appliance deals pushed from Q3 to Q4 and product returning to growth, with the CEO saying 'the optimism comes from what we see already in Q4'. The Nov-2 Q4 guide either confirms that ramp or trims the FY midpoint for the second time this year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY revenue cut on Apr-30-2026: -19.6%. Q3 guide below consensus on Jul-30-2026: -8.2%. On Oct-28-2025, an in-line Q3 with the guide intact: +6.2% (191.72 to 203.56).
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is 27% off its high and roughly 13x FY EPS. If the market believed the $800M Q4, it would trade back toward the pre-April $140-176 range rather than ~149. If it fully expected a trim, puts would be bid, and the 25d skew is negative, with calls bid.
evidence.independence: FY range of $2.77-2.85B from the Q1 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/check-point-software-technologies-q1-earnings-call-highlights-2026-04-30/). Q2 results $674M from the company release (https://www.checkpoint.com/press-releases/check-point-software-reports-2026-second-quarter-financial-results/). The Q4 implication is arithmetic on these company documents.

evidence.text: The +13.85% 20-day run-up is a sector move with no company news: +15% in three sessions (Oct 21-23, 140.85 to 159.03 on 2.4-2.6M shares vs ~1.3M average) on a Morgan Stanley enterprise-security-spending note, PHP vulnerability headlines and UBS/Mizuho target raises to $145, which is still below spot. About half of it has already been given back.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on run-up into prints. Before Oct-25 (+6.2%) the stock had been falling; before Apr-26 (-19.6%) it was ~flat.
evidence.why_not_priced: The UBS and Mizuho targets of $145 sit below the 149 spot, and the rally was sector-wide rather than CHKP-specific. If the rally were fully unwound, the stock would sit near 140, not 149.
evidence.independence: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Check+Point+Software+rises+as+cybersecurity+shares+gain+on+stronger+spending+outlook (2026-10-23, attributes the move to sector rotation and PHP vulns). Short interest is not crowded at 4.9 DTC, so there is no squeeze mechanism against this.

evidence.text: Check Point bought back ~2.5M shares for ~$325M in Q2 2026 (company release) under a $2B program. Continued Q3 repurchase lowers the share count and supports a non-GAAP EPS print at or above the $2.53 top of the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats were sold on all of the last three prints (Q2: $2.55 vs $2.45, -8.2%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: CHKP routinely beats EPS. It is listed so the judges see the EPS line is likely a beat that does not drive the stock.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: The shekel has traded near 30-year highs against the dollar through 2026 (~2.9 NIS/$ in May 2026), raising Check Point's Israeli-shekel cost base in dollars against the year-ago quarter. This is a small operating-margin headwind, mostly inside the Q3 EPS guide set on Jul-30.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to FX on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Inside the guide, so it is largely priced. It is filed as a proxy only.
evidence.independence: https://tradingeconomics.com/israel/currency/news/553476 (shekel 33-year high). This is a proxy; the company has not quantified the Q3 effect.

evidence.text: Q3 2026 cooling demand in Entergy's census regions ran well above normal and above last year. AGA cooling degree days (weighted to AC customers) to 2026-09-26: West South Central cumulative 2,512 vs 2,241 last year (+12.1%) and normal 2,093 (+20%); about 528 CDD in September alone vs about 344 normal. East South Central cumulative +11.1% YoY. National August +22.3% YoY. Entergy booked +$0.06/share of weather vs normal in Q3 2025 and -$0.02 YTD through Q2 2026, so Q3 2026 weather plausibly adds several cents vs a normal-weather consensus of about $1.72.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 had a +$0.06 weather benefit and a narrowed guide; the stock moved +0.46%. Last seven reactions have a median |move| of 1.76%, with 5 of 7 up. Utility weather beats are usually treated as low quality.
evidence.why_not_priced: Sell-side quarterly estimates are usually built on normal weather. If the market had priced the hot August and September, Q3 estimates would have risen over the quarter. Instead chartmill reports Entergy's next-quarter revenue estimate cut 4.2% over three months, and consensus EPS of about $1.72 is +12% on the year ago, in line with the guided growth rate and not above it.
evidence.independence: Company YTD weather figures from the Q2 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65984/000006598426000279/earningsrelease2q26_ex991.htm) give the comparison base. CenterPoint (Houston, same WSC region) booked +$0.03 of favourable weather and usage in its Q3 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001130310/000110465926118963/tm2628051d1_ex99-1.htm). This is a proxy: a regional series, not Entergy's own number.

evidence.text: Three regulated peers that reported after Entergy last spoke beat and lifted outlooks. AEP (2026-10-28): operating EPS $2.23 vs about $2.04 consensus, 2026 guided at or above the top of $6.25-6.55, new 2027/2028 guides, $100B capex plan. CenterPoint (2026-10-27): $0.53 vs about $0.50, raised 2026 guide and a $70.7B plan, with Houston industrial throughput +11% YTD. FirstEnergy beat at $0.98 vs $0.90 and reaffirmed. This sets a sector bar of a beat plus an outlook lift on data-center load.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 raised the longer-term outlook: +1.33%. Q2 2026 affirmed only (with a $2.175B equity raise in the quarter): -4.03%. Q3 2025 narrowed and extended outlooks: +0.46%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. ETR is up 9.3% in 20 days, from about $104-106 around 10-21 to $110.28, which is consistent with the sector re-rating on these prints. evidence.text: Q3 EPS: Q2 gross margin was about 29.9% (Q1 26.8%, Q2 2025 21.5%) and operating margin about 19.6% (Q1 15.6%), with the tax rate already at about 14.7%. Adding $60M of revenue at roughly 50% incremental operating margin gives about $1.08-1.12 adjusted EPS against the $1.05-1.07 consensus. That is a small beat, extending a five-quarter beat streak.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS $0.88 versus $0.76 consensus and revenue $460.1M versus $454.7M. The stock closed +2.2% on 2026-08-04 after trading as low as $206.40 intraday, then fell 11.9% on 08-05. This name has sold its last beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS has already risen from $0.892 to $1.066 over 90 days (24/7), so most of the leverage is in the bar. What remains is a few cents, on a line this stock has not paid for.

evidence.text: A sector shock hit the AI-optics names on 2026-10-29/30. Alphabet reported Q3 free cash flow of -$9.1B against -$3.5B expected, though 2026 capex was unchanged at $195-205B. Intel guided Q4 to $15-16B against $17B expected and fell about 30%. COHR -13%, LITE -10%, AAOI -15%, and TSEM -14.1% to 161.36 with no company news. The print opens on Monday into this momentum.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In the 2026-05-13 print the stock went from a sector-driven dip into +22.6%. On 2026-08-04/05 a broader tech pullback swamped a beat (-11.9% the next day).
evidence.why_not_priced: The Friday close already holds the shock (spot 161.36). What is left is whether de-risking continues into Monday's open, which the +20.7 put skew says the market expects. This is macro-to-company transmission; no Tower customer has cut. Alphabet kept 2026 capex unchanged and expects 2027 capex to rise significantly, so the demand line itself was not cut.
evidence.independence: Alphabet capex unchanged and 2027 to rise significantly (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-google-cloud-revenue-doubles-to-30-7b-as-capex-hits-51-4b/), which cuts against reading this as a demand cut. Intel guide: https://qz.com/intel-stock-falls-revenue-forecast-pc-demand-102926.

The balance sheet funds it: about $1.48B of cash and deposits against $142M of debt, plus $321M of customer advances. Answer to the financing question: the money buys customer-prepaid capacity, so this is close to zero.

evidence.independence: Same 6-K as the guidance and EPS findings; a different line (cash flow).

evidence.text: The Intel New Mexico capacity agreement is in dispute resolution. Intel stated in February 2026 that it does not intend to perform, and the Q2 6-K still lists the dispute as a risk without quantifying it. Tower invested up to $300M in equipment at that site under the 2023 deal. A settlement or impairment could be disclosed with Q3, now that Intel is under fresh pressure (Q4 guide miss, Fab 28 outage).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-02-11, when the Intel non-performance was disclosed with Q4 2025 results: -1.6% close-to-close.
evidence.why_not_priced: The outcome is unknown and either sign is possible: cash compensation, or a write-down of the New Mexico equipment. It is below operating income, and the volumes were rerouted to Fab 7 Japan, so there is no path to the guide. [sizing note removed].
evidence.independence: TrendForce on the rerouting to Japan (https://www.trendforce.com/news/2026/02/13/news-intel-reportedly-backs-out-of-300mm-wafer-deal-with-tower-production-could-move-to-japan/).
